---
title: "Hands-on Simulink Build-Along Workshop"
subtitle: "From control models to circuits and power systems"
---

## Overview
This workshop is a **hands-on, build-along session** designed for Electrical and Electronic Engineering students who want practical exposure to **system modelling and simulation using Simulink**.

Rather than slides or theory-heavy explanations, participants will **build models step by step**, validate results together, and understand how simulation tools are used across **control systems, circuit analysis, and power systems**.

You’ll follow guided instructions, experiment on your own device, and leave with reusable models you can build on in your coursework and projects.

---

## Who this workshop is for
- EEE undergraduate and postgraduate students  
- Students taking (or interested in):
  - Control Systems
  - Circuit Analysis / Electronics
  - Power Systems
- Beginners are welcome — no prior Simulink expertise required

---

## What you’ll learn
By the end of this session, you will be able to:
- Translate mathematical models into **Simulink block diagrams**
- Simulate **basic control system responses**
- Model simple **RC/RLC circuits using Simscape**
- Understand the structure of **three-phase power system simulations**
- Read and interpret simulation results with confidence

---

## Session format
- **Duration:** 2 hours  
- **Style:** Fully interactive, build-along  
- **Format:** Short explanations → live modelling → individual practice  
- **Requirements:** Bring your own laptop

---

## Software requirements
Please ensure the following are installed **before attending**:
- MATLAB
- Simulink
- Simscape  
*(Installation guidance will be provided if needed.)*

## About the event
This workshop is organised by the **Electrical and Electronic Engineering Society (EEESAU)** as part of its technical skills development initiatives.

The goal is to help students bridge the gap between **theory taught in lectures** and **practical engineering workflows used in industry and research**.
